notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass adds an alert to David Kim (user 4), the other IT Support member, reading 'whoever is in the newly assigned group' as every member; dropped because the request speaks of 'an alert notification' and of 'both notifications', which the benchmark's single alert to Emily Watson and its count of exactly two match, so the request does not contradict the benchmark's reading.
disagreement: value: the expected count of ready notifications on case 2: one pass 3, the other 2; chose 2, following the dropped alert (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass has a stay that case 2 keeps approver 2, request_status requested and status awaiting_approval, the other tests the same three cells inside the assignment change; kept the stay, so the change tests what moves and the stay what must not, with the benchmark's approver check carried jointly by both (logged on the assignment requirement).
disagreement: value: org_id in the assignment change: one pass tests org_id = 1, the other leaves it to the anchor as a seed fact; kept org_id = 1 because the benchmark check tests it and nothing contradicts it (logged on the requirement).
Decision path on the seed: HRC-0002 (hr_case 2) sits in Service Desk (group 2) with skills [2] (Benefits Advisor); the rule from Service Desk escalates to Infrastructure Team (group 4), whose only member Michael Rodriguez lacks Benefits Advisor, so the case goes to IT Support (group 1) at priority high. All three groups exist and are active, so no validation failure stops the request.
The reading of a single alert is the point a reviewer is most likely to read differently: 'whoever is in the newly assigned group' could also mean one alert per IT Support member, three notifications in all, which would fail the count of two.
The six seed-fact checks (escalation rule, group memberships, skills, the case's starting state) are weak and are not carried. The task's assigned_to is not tested: the request names only the team and the benchmark does not test it, though the policy would require any assignee to be an active member of IT Support. The policy's 30-120 character limit on short_description is not tested by the benchmark and is left out; LIKE matching is case-insensitive, but 'Escalated' does not satisfy '%Escalation%'. No checklist item rows are required: the request asks for a task of type checklist, and no listed tool writes the checklist table.
The acting user Sarah Chen is an admin; the policy bars admins from routine HR case work but gives them full write access, and the benchmark expects the escalation to be carried out, so the request is treated as permitted.
